c.tagline: Island of temples, surf, and rice terraces

taxi.fareNote: Blue Bird metered; many others unmetered, use apps

emergency.note: 112 also works as a general emergency line in Bali; English-speaking operators are inconsistent, so hotels often help place calls.

hood_landmark.Sanur: the gentle beachfront promenade and calm swimming beach
hood_landmark.Renon: Bajra Sandhi Monument in the Puputan Renon field
hood_landmark.Sesetan: home of the annual Omed-Omedan 'kissing festival'
hood_landmark.Kesiman: Pura Petilan temple, famed for its Pengerebongan trance ceremonies
hood_landmark.Panjer: Plaza Renon mall and its surrounding local eateries

avoid.reason: Bali generally safe — watch scooter bag-snatching, ATM skimming, methanol-tainted drinks and rental-damage/insurance scams

hood_desc: A laid-back beachside area on Denpasar's east coast with a calm lagoon, boardwalk, older resorts and expat cafes; suits families, older travelers and those wanting a mellow seaside base.
Denpasar's spacious government and diplomatic district, leafy and orderly with the Bajra Sandhi monument and jogging parks; suits business visitors and those wanting quiet, upscale local living.
A busy central-south Denpasar neighborhood, local and residential with markets, guesthouses and street food; suits budget travelers wanting authentic city life.
A traditional eastern Denpasar area rich in temples and Balinese family compounds; suits culture seekers wanting an authentic residential and spiritual atmosphere.
A growing residential south-central neighborhood with cafes, co-working spots and easy access to Renon and Sanur; suits digital nomads and longer-stay visitors wanting local convenience.
lodging: Aston Denpasar Hotel and Convention Center
Aston Denpasar Hotel and Convention Center

water.note: Avoid tap water; use bottled, boiled, or filtered water throughout your stay.

transit.pay: Pay onboard with cash or a QRIS e-wallet scan for a flat fare of about Rp 4,400 (~$0.30) per ride. Coverage is limited, so most visitors instead use the Grab or Gojek apps for on-demand cars and scooters, typically Rp 15,000-40,000 (~$1-3) per short trip.
transit.hours: Buses run approximately 5am-9pm with no night service; Grab/Gojek ride-hailing operates 24 hours.
transit.note: Bali is best navigated with Grab/Gojek and scooter or car rentals; Trans Metro Dewata buses are a budget option mainly for fixed corridors around Denpasar, Sanur and Kuta.
